vignette: Sarita, a 70-year-old South Asian woman, has lived much of her life in the shadow of childhood trauma. Growing up, she endured years of physical abuse at the hands of her caregiver, an experience that left deep psychological scars. Sarita’s current distress is rooted in a complex interplay between her negative appraisals and maladaptive coping strategies, both of which have profoundly affected how she recalls and processes the traumatic event. Sarita had come to believe that no one was held accountable for the abuse she endured as a child. This conviction that justice was never served has fueled an intense sense of vigilance and a pervasive feeling that she belongs nowhere. Her belief in her own vulnerability is so strong that it has shaped her day-to-day life, influencing how she processes memories of the trauma. Her hypervigilance is ever-present; even now, as she walks through her neighborhood or works on her photography projects, Sarita feels an overwhelming need to be constantly alert. This constant state of readiness has led her to engage in various maladaptive strategies. She often tries to control her emotions and cover her face with her hands when the memories become too much to bear. These behaviors are deeply intertwined with her struggles with memory recall. When Sarita remembers the traumatic events, she is overwhelmed by a sense of shame that feels as intense now as it did at the time of the abuse. The difficulty in deliberately recalling specific details makes these fragmented memories all the more terrifying and shameful when they do surface. Her efforts to control her emotions and hide her face are responses to the terror brought back by these recollections, which she cannot escape. Sarita's hypervigilance has also affected how she interacts with her environment as a photographer. The bustling streets of her neighborhood can sometimes trigger memories that cause her to retreat into herself, hiding behind her camera rather than engaging with others. Her work often suffers as a result; she has missed deadlines and assignments due to the intrusive thoughts and feelings that arise unexpectedly. Her sense of not belonging anywhere exacerbates these issues. Sarita feels disconnected from her community and even from those few people who know about her past. This isolation has led to further emotional suppression, making it harder for her to deal with the trauma directly. She frequently questions why she was singled out for such abuse, a cycle that keeps her trapped in rumination. The cumulative effect of these experiences is a self-reinforcing loop where Sarita's negative appraisals lead her to adopt maladaptive strategies that further distort and intensify her memory recall. Each time she tries to control her emotions or hide from the memories, it becomes harder for her to confront them directly. What finally brought Sarita to seek help was the realization that her isolation and emotional suppression were becoming unsustainable. She had started to miss out on opportunities in her photography work, and her social life was deteriorating further. Despite her fears, she is now most hopeful that with support, she can begin to break free from this cycle of avoidance and memory distortion. Sarita’s current state is marked by a profound sense of vulnerability and shame, but there is also a glimmer of hope that therapy might offer the tools she needs to reclaim some control over her life.
